How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Moderators started asking for this:

> As a moderator, I want to reuse my quiz at another conference, or share it with a colleague who runs Quizzy too.

The quiz page gets the "Export" link. It opens a page that shows the quiz as JSON inside a `<pre>` element (the only `<pre>` on the page), ready to copy.

`/moderate` gets the "Import quiz" button. It opens a page with a "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button. Importing always creates a new quiz, even if a quiz with the same title exists, and opens its page.

The format:

```json
{
  "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
  "questions": [
    {
      "text": "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
      "active": true,
      "options": [
        {"text": "418", "correct": false},
        {"text": "429", "correct": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `questions` and `options` keep their order.
- On import, `active` is optional (`true` by default), and `correct` is optional (`false` by default).
- The export always writes both, and it writes exactly these keys: the quiz title and its questions, nothing else. The export is only for moving quiz contents.
- Imported questions follow the same rules as the question form.

When the JSON is invalid or breaks a rule, the page shows an error and nothing is imported: not the quiz, not a part of its questions.

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  OptionRow = Data.define(:id, :body, :correct)

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :question

  normalizes :body, with: ->(body) { body.strip }

  before_validation :assign_position, on: :create

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than: 0 }

  def save_with_option_rows(rows)
    non_empty = rows.reject { |r| r.body.to_s.strip.empty? }

    valid?
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if non_empty.size < 2
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if non_empty.none?(&:correct)
    return false if errors.any?

    Question.transaction do
      save!
      kept_ids = []
      non_empty.each_with_index do |row, idx|
        pos = idx + 1
        existing = row.id.present? ? options.find_by(id: row.id) : nil
        if existing
          existing.update!(body: row.body.strip, correct: row.correct, position: pos)
          kept_ids << existing.id
        else
          created = options.create!(body: row.body.strip, correct: row.correct, position: pos)
          kept_ids << created.id
        end
      end
      options.where.not(id: kept_ids).destroy_all
    end
    true
  end

  def move_up!
    move_by(-1)
  end

  def move_down!
    move_by(1)
  end

  private

  def assign_position
    return if position.present?
    self.position = (quiz&.questions&.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end

  def move_by(offset)
    Question.transaction do
      ordered = quiz.questions.order(:position, :id).lock.to_a
      ordered.each_with_index do |q, i|
        q.update_column(:position, i + 1) if q.position != i + 1
      end
      idx = ordered.index(self)
      return false unless idx

      target_idx = idx + offset
      return false if target_idx < 0 || target_idx >= ordered.size

      neighbor = ordered[target_idx]
      my_pos = ordered[idx].position
      neighbor_pos = neighbor.position

      update_column(:position, neighbor_pos)
      neighbor.update_column(:position, my_pos)
      true
    end
  end
end

class QuizImport
  include ActiveModel::Model
  include ActiveModel::Attributes

  attribute :json, :string
  attr_reader :quiz

  def save
    @quiz = nil
    errors.clear

    raw = json.to_s
    if raw.strip.empty?
      errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON can't be blank")
      return false
    end

    data = parse_json(raw)
    return false unless data

    parsed = validate_payload(data)
    return false unless parsed

    persist_quiz(parsed)
  end

  private

  def parse_json(raw)
    data = JSON.parse(raw)
    unless data.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON must be a JSON object")
      return nil
    end
    data
  rescue JSON::ParserError => e
    errors.add(:base, "Invalid JSON: #{e.message}")
    nil
  end

  def validate_payload(data)
    title = data["title"]
    if !title.is_a?(String) || title.strip.empty?
      errors.add(:base, "Title can't be blank")
    end

    unless data.key?("questions") && data["questions"].is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "Questions must be an array")
      return nil
    end

    parsed_questions = data["questions"].each_with_index.filter_map do |q_data, q_idx|
      validate_question(q_data, q_idx + 1)
    end

    return nil if errors.any?

    { title: title.strip, questions: parsed_questions }
  end

  def validate_question(q_data, q_num)
    unless q_data.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{q_num} must be an object")
      return nil
    end

    q_text = q_data["text"]
    if !q_text.is_a?(String) || q_text.strip.empty?
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{q_num}: Question can't be blank")
    end

    if q_data.key?("active")
      active_val = q_data["active"]
      unless active_val == true || active_val == false
        errors.add(:base, "Question #{q_num}: active must be true or false")
      end
    else
      active_val = true
    end

    unless q_data.key?("options") && q_data["options"].is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{q_num}: options must be an array")
      return nil
    end

    options_data = q_data["options"]
    parsed_options = options_data.each_with_index.filter_map do |o_data, o_idx|
      validate_option(o_data, q_num, o_idx + 1)
    end

    if options_data.size < 2
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{q_num}: Add at least two options")
    end

    if parsed_options.none? { |o| o[:correct] == true }
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{q_num}: Mark at least one option as correct")
    end

    { body: q_text.to_s.strip, active: active_val, options: parsed_options }
  end

  def validate_option(o_data, q_num, o_num)
    unless o_data.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{q_num}, option #{o_num} must be an object")
      return nil
    end

    o_text = o_data["text"]
    if !o_text.is_a?(String) || o_text.strip.empty?
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{q_num}, option #{o_num}: text can't be blank")
    end

    if o_data.key?("correct")
      correct_val = o_data["correct"]
      unless correct_val == true || correct_val == false
        errors.add(:base, "Question #{q_num}, option #{o_num}: correct must be true or false")
      end
    else
      correct_val = false
    end

    { body: o_text.to_s.strip, correct: correct_val }
  end

  def persist_quiz(parsed)
    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: parsed[:title])
      parsed[:questions].each_with_index do |pq, q_idx|
        question = @quiz.questions.create!(
          body: pq[:body],
          active: pq[:active],
          position: q_idx + 1
        )
        pq[:options].each_with_index do |po, o_idx|
          question.options.create!(
            body: po[:body],
            correct: po[:correct],
            position: o_idx + 1
          )
        end
      end
    end
    true
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
    @quiz = nil
    e.record.errors.full_messages.each { |msg| errors.add(:base, msg) }
    false
  end
end

# Quizzy Architecture Notes

## Data Model (Release 1: Moderator Prep)
- `Quiz` (`title`) has_many `Question` ordered by `position, id`.
- `Question` (`quiz_id`, `body`, `position`, `active`) has_many `Option` ordered by `position, id`.
- `Option` (`question_id`, `body`, `correct`, `position`).

## Design & Assets
- Design tokens, layout, and component classes live in `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` (adapted from `docs/mockups/quizzy.css`) with `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2`.
- Lists (`quiz-list`, `question-list`) use semantic `<ul>` / `<li>` items so each item's controls sit inside its `<li>`.
- Confirmation dialogs use `data-turbo-confirm` (native `window.confirm()`).

## Moderator Area & Auth
- Everything under `/moderate` inherits from `Moderate::BaseController` and enforces HTTP Basic Authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using SHA-256 + `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Preview (`/moderate/quizzes/:id/preview`) is client-side via Stimulus (`preview_controller.js`) over active questions only; no preview answers are persisted.

## Quiz Export & Import
- Export (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export`) serializes `Quiz#export_payload` with `JSON.pretty_generate` inside a single `<pre>` element, writing only `title`, `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options`), and `options` (`text`, `correct`) in preserved order.
- Import (`GET /moderate/quizzes/import`, `POST /moderate/quizzes/import`) is handled by `QuizImport` (`ActiveModel::Model`), validating structure and question/option rules atomically inside a transaction so invalid payloads import nothing. `active` defaults to `true` and `correct` defaults to `false` when omitted.
